Onboard Rebellious: Inside the 50m Mangusta 165 REV superyacht

Written by Ann Yabut
Fri, 30 Oct 2026 | 08:15
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:40
Instaread

SuperYacht Times steps onboard the 49.95-metre Mangusta 165 REV motor yacht Rebellious, where sporty lines meet modern luxury. Delivered in 2022, she is currently for sale as an open listing.

Advertisement
Built by Italian shipyard Mangusta Yachts, Rebellious features exterior design by Lobanov Design, with interior design and naval architecture crafted in-house by her builder. Constructed with a GRP hull and superstructure, she has a beam of 9.29-metres and an interior volume of 499 GT.
On the outside, Rebellious has a streamlined exterior with her white hull contrasted by sweeping black glazing along her superstructure. Her low-profile silhouette and sculpted lines reflect the performance-oriented design of the Mangusta 165 REV series, while her expansive deck areas serve as a perfect setting for outdoor relaxation and entertaining.
Forward, her foredeck centres around a striking Jacuzzi surrounded by large sunpads, alongside lounging and alfresco dining spots tucked under a retractable canopy. Rich red cushions pop against the crisp white furnishings, adding a vibrant splash of color to her otherwise restrained palette.  
Her sundeck is an outdoor retreat that encourages socialising and relaxing, featuring a plush curved sofa arranged around a coffee table, a bar counter with stools, and dedicated gym equipment. A sculptural black hardtop provides partial shade, contrasting with the light decking and white upholstery.
Aft on her main deck, built-in seating and a dining area create a perfect area for gatherings while the ocean breeze gently stirs, complete with seamless access to her stern platform. Below, her beach club offers a more intimate waterside sanctuary, housing a soothing steam room and steps that lead directly into the pristine waters.
Moving inside, Rebellious welcomes guests with a contemporary interior defined by sculptural furnishings, pale tones and sweeping glazing that floods the space with natural light. Her main saloon is arranged with a spacious lounge forward, where a curved cream-coloured sofa sits alongside meticulously crafted coffee tables. A marble feature wall introduces texture and contrast, while mirrored ceiling accents and integrated lighting reinforce her modern aesthetic.
A dedicated dining area occupies the aft section of the saloon, boasting a marble-topped table flanked by sophisticated upholstered chairs. Glass doors connect the aft terrace to her living spaces, creating a seamless flow between her indoor and outdoor entertaining areas.
Spanning nearly 500 GT, accommodation onboard Rebellious is arranged for up to 12 guests across six staterooms. Notably, her configuration comprises a full-beam, 92-square-metre split-level master suite, which boasts sculptural furnishings, large windows, and ambient lighting, alongside an ensuite bathroom with a central glass-enclosed shower.
Moreover, her five remaining guest staterooms are located on the lower deck, all ensuite. Dedicated quarters are available for up to 10 crew members.
In terms of performance, Rebellious is powered by four MTU engines, paired with Kamewa waterjet propulsion, propelling her to a top speed of 36 knots and a cruising speed of 30 knots.
All images provided courtesy of Smart Yachts.

US yacht builder Lyman-Morse opens $4m composites centre
US yacht builder Lyman-Morse has opened a new composites centre in Maine and launched a dedicated Defense division, reflecting two rising business interests in the growth of composites demand and the builder’s close relationship with the US Department of Defense (DoD). The Maine-headquartered company said its new Advanced Composites Centre marked its third major capital investment at its Elltee Circle campus in the state, providing an almost 1,400 square-metre site for large-scale, complex composite construction. The site features specialised equipment such as two 59-metre wide overhead cranes, integrated vacuum systems, and compressors for building yachts from composite materials, which combine fibres and resin using laminate architecture to create a lightweight structure. Construction of the $4 million (€3.6 million) centre began in May 2026 after Lyman-Morse received an almost $2 million award from the Maine Technology Institute, granted in the interest of adding jobs in the area and supporting the state’s supply chain resilience.
